1	# Publishing the images, and moving a release channel.
2	#
3	# This is the only thing in the pipeline that writes to the registry, and the
4	# registry is the only thing the deployment hosts read. Nothing in CI can
5	# reach a VPS: there is no SSH key here, no deploy credential and no inbound
6	# endpoint to call. A host decides for itself, every minute, whether what it
7	# runs matches its channel (deploy/hetzner/bin/apivo-reconcile).
8	#
9	# Two entry points, one body:
10	#
11	#   push to main    version main-<sha>, channel `qa`. Every merge, unattended.
12	#   workflow_call   release.yml passes the tag and the channel it earned.
13	#
14	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
15	# The order of the last two steps is the safety property
16	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
17	#
18	# Images are pushed under an immutable `sha-<commit>` tag FIRST, then the
19	# artefact that is now in the registry is run and made to say its own version,
20	# and only then does the channel tag move. A build whose stamp did not land
21	# never becomes the thing an environment tracks — it sits in the registry
22	# addressable by commit, which is exactly what you want when working out why
23	# it was rejected.
24	name: publish
25	
26	on:
27	  push:
28	    branches: [main]
29	  workflow_call:
30	    inputs:
31	      version:
32	        description: "The version to stamp into the images (a release tag)."
33	        type: string
34	        required: true
35	      channel:
36	        description: "The channel tag to move once the images are proven: staging or prod."
37	        type: string
38	        required: true
39	    outputs:
40	      api_digest:
41	        description: "The digest the api image was published under."
42	        value: ${{ jobs.publish.outputs.api_digest }}
43	      web_digest:
44	        description: "The digest the web image was published under."
45	        value: ${{ jobs.publish.outputs.web_digest }}
46	
47	permissions:
48	  contents: read
49	
50	concurrency:
51	  # Never cancelled. A cancelled publish can leave a channel tag pointing at
52	  # an image whose proof step never ran, and every host tracking that channel
53	  # would take it within the minute.
54	  group: publish-${{ inputs.channel || 'qa' }}
55	
56	jobs:
57	  # On main only: the full CI matrix before anything is published, by calling
58	  # ci.yml rather than copying its jobs. ci.yml no longer triggers on pushes
59	  # to main itself — this call replaced that trigger, so the matrix runs once
60	  # per merge and an image can only exist for a commit that passed it.
61	  #
62	  # When release.yml calls this workflow the job is skipped: release.yml has
63	  # already run the same matrix on the tagged commit, and running it twice
64	  # would say nothing new about the same tree.
65	  #
66	  # The discriminator is `inputs.version`, NOT github.event_name: a reusable
67	  # workflow sees the CALLER's event, and release.yml is itself triggered by
68	  # a push (of a tag), so an event_name test would run the whole matrix a
69	  # second time on every release.
70	  verify:
71	    if: inputs.version == ''
72	    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml
73	
74	  publish:
75	    needs: verify
76	    # `always()` so the workflow_call path (where `verify` is skipped) still
77	    # runs, while a genuinely failed matrix still stops it.
78	    if: always() && (needs.verify.result == 'success' || needs.verify.result == 'skipped')
79	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
80	    timeout-minutes: 45
81	    permissions:
82	      contents: read
83	      packages: write
84	    outputs:
85	      api_digest: ${{ steps.api.outputs.digest }}
86	      web_digest: ${{ steps.web.outputs.digest }}
87	    steps:
88	      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
89	
90	      - name: Decide the version and the channel
91	        id: what
92	        env:
93	          INPUT_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
94	          INPUT_CHANNEL: ${{ inputs.channel }}
95	        run: |
96	          # Through the environment rather than interpolated into the script:
97	          # a caller's input is data, and this job holds a registry token.
98	          if [ -n "$INPUT_VERSION" ]; then
99	            version="$INPUT_VERSION"
100	            channel="$INPUT_CHANNEL"
101	          else
102	            # An unreleased build says so in its own name. `dev` would be
103	            # honest but useless — every QA build would be called the same
104	            # thing, and "is QA running my merge yet?" would have no answer.
105	            version="main-$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
106	            channel="qa"
107	          fi
108	          case "$channel" in
109	          qa | staging | prod) ;;
110	          *)
111	            echo "::error::'$channel' is not a channel; the channels are qa, staging and prod"
112	            exit 1
113	            ;;
114	          esac
115	          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
116	          echo "channel=$channel" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
117	
118	          # An image reference must be lowercase, and an owner need not be:
119	          # this repository is Nomos-N4s/apivo-news, so the obvious
120	          # ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }} is `ghcr.io/Nomos-N4s/...` — an
121	          # invalid reference that fails the build with "repository name must
122	          # be lowercase". Workflow expressions have no toLower, so it is done
123	          # here and exported for every later step.
124	          registry="ghcr.io/$(printf '%s' "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
125	          echo "REGISTRY=$registry" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
126	          echo "publishing $version to the '$channel' channel as $registry"
127	
128	      # The stamp channel the Dockerfile reads: a VERSION file at the context
129	      # root (git-ignored, never committed), turned into
130	      # -ldflags "-X main.version=…". It exists because the builder cannot be
131	      # relied on to pass a build arg — it is the one channel every builder
132	      # shares.
133	      - name: Stamp the version into the build context
134	        run: printf '%s' '${{ steps.what.outputs.version }}' > VERSION
135	
136	      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
137	
138	      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
139	        with:
140	          registry: ghcr.io
141	          username: ${{ github.actor }}
142	          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
143	
144	      # Both images carry the version as a standard OCI label. That label is
145	      # not decoration: the reconciler on each host reads it off the image to
146	      # learn what the artefact calls itself, and then requires the running
147	      # api to serve exactly that. It is how a deploy proves it rolled
148	      # forward instead of assuming it.
149	      - name: Build and push the api image
150	        id: api
151	        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
152	        with:
153	          context: .
154	          push: true
155	          tags: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/api:sha-${{ github.sha }}
156	          labels: |
157	            org.opencontainers.image.version=${{ steps.what.outputs.version }}
158	            org.opencontainers.image.revision=${{ github.sha }}
159	            org.opencontainers.image.source=${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}
160	          # Layer cache in the registry itself, so a merge that touches only
161	          # Go source does not re-download the module graph.
162	          cache-from: type=gha
163	          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
164	
165	      - name: Build and push the web image
166	        id: web
167	        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
168	        with:
169	          context: web
170	          push: true
171	          tags: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/web:sha-${{ github.sha }}
172	          labels: |
173	            org.opencontainers.image.version=${{ steps.what.outputs.version }}
174	            org.opencontainers.image.revision=${{ github.sha }}
175	            org.opencontainers.image.source=${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}
176	          cache-from: type=gha
177	          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
178	
179	      # The artefact that is now in the registry — not a local build that
180	      # resembles it — is made to say its own version. A stamp that did not
181	      # land fails here, with the channel tag still pointing wherever it
182	      # pointed before, so no environment ever sees this build.
183	      - name: Prove the published image names its own version
184	        env:
185	          VERSION: ${{ steps.what.outputs.version }}
186	          DIGEST: ${{ steps.api.outputs.digest }}
187	        run: |
188	          got=$(docker run --rm "$REGISTRY/api@$DIGEST" version)
189	          if [ "$got" != "apivo version $VERSION" ]; then
190	            echo "::error::the published image reports '$got', expected 'apivo version $VERSION' — the version stamp did not land. The channel tag was NOT moved; nothing will deploy this build."
191	            exit 1
192	          fi
193	          echo "stamp proof: $got"
194	
195	      # Moving the channel IS the deploy. Every host tracking it takes the new
196	      # digest within a minute, with no further instruction from here.
197	      #
198	      # `imagetools create` re-points a tag at an existing manifest without
199	      # pulling or rebuilding anything, so the digest a channel names is
200	      # always a digest that was proven above.
201	      - name: Move the ${{ steps.what.outputs.channel }} channel
202	        env:
203	          CHANNEL: ${{ steps.what.outputs.channel }}
204	          API_DIGEST: ${{ steps.api.outputs.digest }}
205	          WEB_DIGEST: ${{ steps.web.outputs.digest }}
206	        run: |
207	          docker buildx imagetools create --tag "$REGISTRY/api:$CHANNEL" "$REGISTRY/api@$API_DIGEST"
208	          docker buildx imagetools create --tag "$REGISTRY/web:$CHANNEL" "$REGISTRY/web@$WEB_DIGEST"
209	
210	      - name: Summarise
211	        env:
212	          VERSION: ${{ steps.what.outputs.version }}
213	          CHANNEL: ${{ steps.what.outputs.channel }}
214	          API_DIGEST: ${{ steps.api.outputs.digest }}
215	          WEB_DIGEST: ${{ steps.web.outputs.digest }}
216	        run: |
217	          {
218	            echo "## Published $VERSION to the \`$CHANNEL\` channel"
219	            echo
220	            echo "| Image | Digest |"
221	            echo "| --- | --- |"
222	            echo "| api | \`$API_DIGEST\` |"
223	            echo "| web | \`$WEB_DIGEST\` |"
224	            echo
225	            echo "Every host tracking \`$CHANNEL\` rolls to this within a minute."
226	            echo "Ask what is actually serving with \`sh scripts/env_status.sh\`."
227	          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

=== release_semver.sh ===
#!/bin/sh
# The one definition of "a release version" (issue #119), sourced by
# release_guard.sh (which refuses anything else) and release_notes.sh (which
# measures the notes from the previous one). Two copies of this rule would
# drift, and drift here means the notes are measured from a tag the guard
# would never have released.
#
# The pattern is SemVer 2.0.0's own grammar with the repository's mandatory
# "v" prefix: no leading zeroes in the numeric identifiers (v01.2.3 and
# v1.2.3-01 are not versions), no empty dot-separated identifiers
# (v1.2.3-alpha..1 is not a version), build metadata allowed after "+".
#
# This file only defines functions; sourcing it runs nothing.

# release_semver_ok <name>: true when <name> is a strict semver release tag.
release_semver_ok() {
    printf '%s' "$1" | grep -q -E '^v(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(-(0|[1-9][0-9]*|[0-9]*[A-Za-z-][0-9A-Za-z-]*)(\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*|[0-9]*[A-Za-z-][0-9A-Za-z-]*))*)?(\+[0-9A-Za-z-]+(\.[0-9A-Za-z-]+)*)?$'
}

# release_semver_prerelease <name>: true when <name> carries a pre-release
# part (v0.2.0-rc.1). Build metadata is stripped first, because the "-" that
# matters is the one before "+": v1.2.3+build-7 is a stable release.
release_semver_prerelease() {
    case "${1%%+*}" in
    *-*) return 0 ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}

=== release_guard.sh ===
#!/bin/sh
# The release gate (issue #119): a release may be cut ONLY from an annotated
# semver tag whose commit is already merged to main. Anything else - a
# lightweight tag, a tag on unmerged work, a name that is not semver - is
# refused with a message naming exactly what to fix.
#
# A tag that has already been released may be released again - that is the
# rollback - but only if it still names the same commit.
#
# Usage: release_guard.sh <tag> [main-ref] [released-commit]
#
# main-ref defaults to origin/main (what the release workflow checks
# against); the tests pass a local ref instead.
#
# released-commit is what the already-published GitHub Release for this tag
# records as the commit it was cut from, and it is the one thing here that
# git alone cannot answer. The workflow looks it up (gh release view) and
# passes it in, so this script stays pure git and stays testable:
#
#   ""         no Release exists for this tag yet
#   <sha>      the commit the published Release names
#   unknown    a Release exists but records no commit
#
# Output is one line stating the verdict; the exit code is the verdict.
# ::error:: markers surface the reason in the GitHub Actions annotations UI
# and are plain text anywhere else.
set -eu

if [ "$#" -lt 1 ] || [ "$#" -gt 3 ]; then
    echo "usage: $0 <tag> [main-ref] [released-commit]" >&2
    exit 2
fi

TAG="$1"
MAIN_REF="${2:-origin/main}"
RELEASED_COMMIT="${3:-}"

. "$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)/release_semver.sh"

# Semver shape first: vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with optional pre-release/build
# metadata (v1.2.3, v1.2.3-rc.1, v1.2.3+exp), by SemVer 2.0.0's own grammar
# (release_semver.sh). The push trigger pattern is looser than real semver,
# so the guard re-checks it strictly.
if ! release_semver_ok "$TAG"; then
    echo "::error::'$TAG' is not a semver tag (vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, optional -pre/+build, no leading zeroes, no empty identifiers); releases are cut only from semver tags" >&2
    exit 1
fi

# The tag must exist here and be annotated: an annotated tag is its own git
# object of type "tag" carrying tagger and message - the deliberate release
# act. A lightweight tag resolves straight to type "commit".

    echo "::error::tag '$TAG' does not exist in this checkout; the release workflow needs a full fetch (fetch-depth: 0)" >&2

fi
if [ "$TYPE" != "tag" ]; then
    echo "::error::tag '$TAG' is lightweight (points straight at a $TYPE); a release tag must be annotated: git tag -d $TAG && git tag -a $TAG -m 'release $TAG' <commit>" >&2
    exit 1
fi

# The tagged commit must be reachable from main: a release of unmerged work
# is refused. merge-base --is-ancestor answers exactly that question.
COMMIT=$(git rev-parse "refs/tags/$TAG^{commit}")
if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$COMMIT" "$MAIN_REF"; then
    echo "::error::tag '$TAG' points at $COMMIT, which is not reachable from $MAIN_REF; merge the work to main first - unmerged work is never released" >&2
    exit 1
fi

# A version, once published, names one commit forever. Re-releasing the same
# tag is legitimate and documented - it is how a rollback works - but only
# while the tag still points where the published Release says it was cut
# from. A force-moved tag would otherwise ship different code under a version
# the world has already seen, with release notes describing the old commit.
case "$RELEASED_COMMIT" in
"")
    : # No Release for this tag yet: nothing published to contradict.
    ;;
unknown)
    echo "::error::a GitHub Release for '$TAG' exists but records no commit, so nothing here can prove the tag still names the code that was released; this pipeline stamps every Release with its commit, so the Release was made by hand - check it and re-create it (gh release delete '$TAG'), or cut a new version. Nothing was deployed." >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
"$COMMIT")
    echo "release guard: '$TAG' is an annotated tag on $COMMIT, reachable from $MAIN_REF; re-releasing the commit its published Release already names (rollback or re-run)"
    exit 0
    ;;
*)
    echo "::error::tag '$TAG' now points at $COMMIT, but the published GitHub Release for '$TAG' was cut from $RELEASED_COMMIT: the tag has moved. A released version names one commit forever - deploying this would ship different code under a version that is already public, described by release notes written for the old commit. Cut a new version instead. Nothing was deployed." >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# Where each environment answers. Committed, and the ONLY place these are
# written down.
#
# Nothing here is a secret — a public base URL is public by construction —
# and putting it in git rather than in a settings screen is the same rule
# this repository already holds for its deployment configuration: a value
# that lives only in a dashboard is a value with no history, no review and no
# diff when it changes. Three things read this file:
#
#   .github/workflows/release.yml   to know where to probe a release, and to
#                                   REFUSE a release to a channel whose URL
#                                   is empty
#   .github/workflows/preview.yml   to print a pull request's preview URL
#   scripts/env_status.sh           to answer "what is actually running
#                                   where", for anyone or anything without a
#                                   shell on a host
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE DOMAINS, AND WHY TWO OF THESE ARE STILL EMPTY
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
#   apivo.com   production
#   reapie.com  staging
#   ra1ze.com   QA, and every per-pull-request preview beneath it
#
# That assignment is settled. What is NOT settled is whether those hosts
# answer, and only two of these four values are safe to set before they do.
#
# An empty release URL is not a gap in this file — it is the guard in
# release.yml that refuses to publish images and move a channel tag toward an
# environment that is not there. Writing a URL in before the host serves
# would delete that guard silently: the tag would move, nothing would consume
# it, and the failure would surface as a probe timeout after the fact. So the
# two values that gate a release stay empty until their host answers, and the
# two that gate nothing are set now.

# QA — every push to main, within about a minute of the images being
# published. Set now: nothing gates on it. Until the host is provisioned,
# `make env-status` simply reports QA as down, which is true.
APIVO_QA_URL=https://ra1ze.com

# Release candidates only: v0.2.0-rc.1 and friends.
#
# EMPTY UNTIL STAGING ANSWERS. The domain is reapie.com and the host is the
# same VPS as QA, so this becomes:
#     APIVO_STAGING_URL=https://reapie.com
# in the same change that records the box as provisioned — not before.
APIVO_STAGING_URL=

# Final semver tags, behind an approval gate.
#
# EMPTY ON PURPOSE, and for longer. There is no production VPS, no production
# Supabase project and no production DNS record; the domain is reserved
# (apivo.com) and nothing else about it exists. Filling this in is the last
# step of provisioning that host, and it is what makes a final release
# possible — see docs/ENVIRONMENTS.md.
APIVO_PROD_URL=

# The suffix per-pull-request previews are served under, so a preview lives at
# pr-142.ra1ze.com. Empty means previews are not served; CI still publishes
# their images and says so, and no host picks them up.
#
# Set now, because this gates nothing either: it only decides whether
# preview.yml prints a URL or says no preview host is configured.
#
# The origin certificate must cover BOTH ra1ze.com and *.ra1ze.com — the apex
# is QA and the wildcard is every preview. A Cloudflare Origin Certificate
# takes both alongside the other names, so this costs no ACME and no DNS
# token on the host.
APIVO_PREVIEW_DOMAIN=ra1ze.com

# Deployment topology: root cause and fixes

## Context

QA is the only environment that has ever deployed, it is currently down, and
while it was up it sometimes served two different builds alternately. Staging
and production have never released. Previews are unreliable. This plan names
the causes and fixes them.

Right now (from the probe you ran):

- `/` returns **503 with a fully rendered page** — that is `web`'s own
  `apiUnavailable` branch. The web container is healthy and doing its job.
- `/healthz`, `/readyz` and every `/api/v1/*` return **502 via Caddy** — Caddy
  is up and has no upstream. The api container is not accepting connections.

**Your OpenBao inference is wrong, and it is worth saying so before anything
is built on it.** `#591` is already merged to `main`
(`dd7bfc4`, `8d079d1`, `7a83698`) and the vault is **optional by
construction**: `cmd/apivo/vault.go:32-38` returns `nil, nil` when
`PAYOUT_VAULT_URL` is unset, and `cmd/apivo/main.go:769-776` documents that
as "not a failure" — `POST /payout-destinations` answers 503 and everything
else keeps working. A missing vault cannot stop the api booting. The
`xcoder/openbao-on-qa` branch is unmerged and is not implicated.

---

## The five root causes

### RC1 — `api` is gated on Postgres; `web` is gated on nothing

`deploy/hetzner/compose/docker-compose.local-db.yml:97-102`

```yaml
  api:
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
```

`web` declares no `depends_on` at all
(`deploy/hetzner/compose/docker-compose.yml:75-146`).

If QA's Postgres is unhealthy or gone, compose **will not start the api**,
while `web` comes up regardless. Caddy then 502s `/api/v1/*`, `/healthz` and
`/readyz` (`deploy/hetzner/caddy/snippets.caddy:96-100`) and the web renders
its own 503. **That is exactly the signature you observed**, and it is the
first thing to check on the box.

### RC2 — a failed rollout rebuilds the *whole* stack, twice, every tick — this is the "two versions"

`deploy/hetzner/bin/apivo-reconcile:407-420` and `:451-465`.

`roll_out()` runs one `compose up -d --wait` over **both** services. When the
api fails, `roll_out` returns 1 and the rollback path calls `roll_out` **again**
with the previous digests — recreating `web` as well, which was never at
fault. Then:

- `record_state` never runs, so `current` still names the old digests
  (`:427`).
- The next timer tick (60 s, `apivo-reconcile@.timer:30`) sees
  `RUNNING_API != API_DIGEST` and rolls forward again.

So a broken api puts the environment into a **permanent oscillation**: web is
recreated on the new image, fails, is recreated on the old image, and repeats
every 1–4 minutes for as long as the channel points at the failing build. The
script's own message says the quiet part out loud (`:462`): *"The channel still
points at the broken build, so the next tick will try it again."* Nothing
remembers that a digest already failed, and nothing backs off.

**A reader refreshing during that cycle sees two different builds. That is the
"two versions at the same time".** It is not a proxy bug, not a cache, and not
a race — the host is genuinely alternating between them on a timer.

Ruled out by evidence: Caddy has exactly one upstream per handle and zero
load-balancing, retry or failover directives (`snippets.caddy:96-160`);
`container_name` is fixed everywhere so two versions cannot run concurrently
in one project; the Cloudflare Worker is deployed nowhere (`ci.yml:686-687`
is `--dry-run`).

### RC3 — images are automated; everything else on a host is not

`apivo-reconcile` converges **images only**. The Caddyfiles, every compose
file, the systemd units, and the reconciler scripts themselves are copied by
`deploy/hetzner/provision.sh`, which a human runs over SSH. No workflow ships
anything to a host — there is no ssh/scp/rsync step in `.github/workflows/`.

That makes every change under `deploy/hetzner/**` a silent no-op until someone
remembers. Concretely stale on any host provisioned before them:

- `snippets.caddy:96` — `/api/v1/*` instead of `/api/*` (#546, 2026-09-07).
- `docker-compose.yml:132` — the brand directory mount (#547).
- `docker-compose.edge.preprod.yml:33` — Caddy joining `preview-edge`. Its own
  comment records this exact regression: *"every preview answers 502 with its
  containers sitting there healthy."*
- `apivo-reconcile:166-169` — the web-certificate precondition.
- `apivo-previews:503-507` — pull-before-up, without which a preview serves
  its first commit forever.

Nothing detects the drift. `apivoctl status` reports containers, not config.

### RC4 — staging and production are gated shut by a committed empty string

`deploy/hetzner/environments.env:48` `APIVO_STAGING_URL=` and `:57`
`APIVO_PROD_URL=`. `release.yml:169-182` refuses any release to a channel whose
URL is empty, **before** verify and publish. So every `v*` tag push dies in the
`guard` job.

This is why only QA works. It is the intended guard doing its job — but
`docs/ENVIRONMENTS.md:24-26` says staging's host is provisioned and answering
on `https://reapie.com`, so the guard is now the only thing left. The repo has
**one tag ever** (`v0.1.0`, 2026-08-16) and `origin/main` is **1072 commits**
past it. Nothing downstream of a tag — semver validation, the approval, the
channel move, the probe — has ever executed.

### RC5 — the version identity is incoherent, so skew is undetectable

- `publish.yml:207-208` moves the two channel tags in **two separate calls**.
- `apivo-reconcile:338-341` guards that skew by comparing OCI labels — but
  `image_version()` (`:313-317`) falls back to the literal `dev` when the label
  is missing, so two unlabelled images compare **equal** and the guard passes.
- A half-completed channel move turns into a **permanent silent stall** at
  `exit 0`, once a minute, forever. Nothing escalates it.
- `publish.yml:183-193` proves only the **api** stamp. `web/Dockerfile` has no
  build-time stamp at all.
- The frontend's version is a **runtime env var** set from the *api* image's
  label (`apivo-reconcile:319,354` → `docker-compose.yml:94`). The running web
  bundle's own identity is never reported anywhere.
- `sha-<commit>` is documented as immutable (`publish.yml:18`) but is
  **overwritten** when a release tag lands on a commit already published from
  main (`publish.yml:155` uses `github.sha` on both paths).

---

## The work

### Phase 0 — get QA back (on the box, before any code change)

```sh
apivoctl pause qa                       # stop the oscillation taking the evidence
docker ps -a --filter name=apivo-qa-
docker inspect --format '{{.State.Health.Status}}' apivo-qa-postgres
docker logs --tail 100 apivo-qa-postgres
docker logs --tail 100 apivo-qa-api
journalctl -u apivo-reconcile@qa --since '2 hours ago' | tail -60
df -h && free -m                        # a full disk or OOM is the usual cause
```

The journal is JSON per line (`apivo-reconcile:55-62`); look for
`rollout_failed`, `rollback_failed`, `version_skew`, `digest_mismatch`. Fix
what it names, then `apivoctl resume qa`.

Also re-run `provision.sh` on that host — it is idempotent — because RC3 means
it is very likely several fixes behind.

### Phase 1 — stop the oscillation (`deploy/hetzner/bin/apivo-reconcile`)

1. **Remember a failed digest and refuse to retry it.** Write the failing
   `API_DIGEST`/`WEB_DIGEST` pair to `$STATE_DIR/failed` on a rollout failure;
   at the top of the tick, if the resolved pair equals `failed`, log once and
   `exit 0`. Clear the file whenever the resolved pair differs. This turns
   "retry a known-bad build every minute forever" into "hold the last good
   version and say so".
2. **Do not roll `web` back when only `api` failed.** Have `roll_out` return
   *which* verification failed and restore only that service, so a healthy
   frontend is not recreated onto an older build. This is the direct fix for
   the two-versions symptom.
3. **Make the skew guard fail closed.** In `image_version()`, treat an absent
   or `<no value>` label as an error rather than substituting `dev` — two
   unlabelled images must not compare equal.
4. **Escalate a persistent stall.** `version_skew` (`:338-341`) currently exits
   0 forever. After N consecutive skew ticks, exit non-zero so systemd marks
   the unit failed and the state is visible.

Extend `deploy/hetzner/bin/apivo-reconcile_test.sh` for each: it already stubs
the registry and the daemon, and already covers skew at `:331-351`.

### Phase 2 — close the config-delivery gap (RC3)

Add a **config revision** the host records and reports:

- `provision.sh` writes the checked-out commit to
  `/etc/apivo/config-revision` when it installs files.
- `apivoctl status` prints it beside the running versions.
- Optionally: `apivo-reconcile` compares it against a value carried in the api
  image's OCI labels and logs a warning when the host's deploy config is older
  than the build it is being asked to run.

This does not automate delivery — the no-SSH-from-CI property is deliberate and
worth keeping — it makes the drift *visible*, which is the actual defect.

Also add `APIVO_PREVIEW_DOMAIN` to `deploy/hetzner/env/edge.env.example` (it is
missing at `:39-48`, and `Caddyfile.preprod:81` uses it in a site address —
Caddy refuses to start on an unset site variable, which takes QA and staging
down with previews).

### Phase 3 — unblock staging, then production (RC4)

One PR, in this order:

1. Verify `https://reapie.com/healthz` answers from the host (it will 502 until
   a release lands — that is expected).
2. Set `APIVO_STAGING_URL=https://reapie.com` in
   `deploy/hetzner/environments.env:48`.
3. Cut `v0.2.0-rc.1` as an **annotated, signed** tag on a merged commit and let
   `release.yml` run end to end. This exercises the guard, the notes, the
   channel move and the probe for the first time.
4. Leave `APIVO_PROD_URL` empty until a production host exists. Confirm the
   `production` GitHub Environment exists **with reviewers** — `release.yml:206`
   names it, and if it does not exist the approval gate is decoration.

`docs/RELEASING.md:23` claims all three URLs are empty; QA's is not. Fix that
line in the same PR.

### Phase 4 — one coherent version identity (RC5)

- Stamp the web at build time (a `VERSION` build arg into `web/Dockerfile`,
  surfaced as a `PUBLIC_APP_VERSION` default baked into the image) so the
  frontend can report **its own** identity rather than the api's.
- Extend `publish.yml:183-193` to prove the **web** image's stamp too.
- Move both channel tags in one `imagetools create` invocation, or make the
  second failure fail the job loudly so a half-move cannot be silent.
- Stop reusing `sha-<commit>`: on the release path tag the image
  `v<semver>` as well, so a released artefact has an immutable name.
- Have `scripts/env_status.sh` report the web's version alongside the api's,
  so "two versions" becomes a thing the tooling can *say*.

### Phase 5 — previews

- Pin previews by **digest** like every named environment
  (`apivo-previews:361-362`, `:503-505` use mutable tags).
- Add `--wait` to the converge branch (`apivo-previews:513-516`); create uses it
  (`:372`) and converge does not, so a converge that starts a broken container
  reports success.
- Set `PREVIEW_CLEANUP_TOKEN` — without it `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot delete package
  versions (`preview.yml:57-68`), closed PRs keep their tags, and the cap
  (`APIVO_PREVIEW_MAX=5`, newest-first) evicts *live* previews in favour of dead
  ones.
- Check the Cloudflare wildcard `*.ra1ze.com` is **orange-clouded**.
  `docs/RUNBOOK.md:107-113` records this exact failure: a grey-clouded wildcard
  sends the browser to the VPS IP, which the firewall admits only from
  Cloudflare ranges — *"the symptom is previews timing out while QA works."*
- Call `k8s-topology.yml` and `make-targets.yml` from `publish.yml`; both
  declare `workflow_call` and nothing calls them, so they gate pull requests but
  not the path that deploys to QA (`k8s-topology.yml:20-25` admits this).

### Phase 6 — documentation that currently contradicts itself

`docs/ENVIRONMENTS.md:124` (previews "point at nothing at all") vs `:588` and
the code; `README.md:146-150` (QA "not yet" provisioned) vs
`ENVIRONMENTS.md:17,20`; `RELEASING.md:208-209` (one Supabase project) vs
`ENVIRONMENTS.md:63-67` (two). `deploy/k8s/*-deployment.yaml` reference
`:latest`, a tag nothing writes.

---

## Verification

**Unit / CI, from this checkout — no host needed:**

```sh
make hetzner-validate                      # compose config, both Caddyfiles, shellcheck
sh deploy/hetzner/bin/apivo-reconcile_test.sh
sh deploy/hetzner/bin/apivo-previews_test.sh
sh scripts/release_guard_test.sh && sh scripts/release_notes_test.sh
make vet && make test-unit
```

The reconciler suite stubs the registry and the docker daemon, so Phase 1 is
fully provable without a VPS. Add a case for each new behaviour: a repeated
failing digest is refused, a healthy `web` is not recreated when only `api`
fails, an unlabelled image fails the skew guard closed.

**On the host, after Phase 0/2:**

```sh
apivoctl status                            # versions + the new config revision
sh scripts/env_status.sh                   # what each environment SERVES
journalctl -u apivo-reconcile@qa -f        # one quiet JSON line per tick
```

QA is fixed when `env_status.sh` reports one version, `/healthz` answers 200,
and the journal shows quiet ticks rather than a rollout every minute.

**End to end, Phase 3:** push `v0.2.0-rc.1` and watch `release.yml` run
guard → verify → publish → release → probe, then `sh scripts/env_status.sh`
shows staging serving that exact tag.

# Deployment topology: root cause and fixes

## Context

QA is the only environment that has ever deployed, it is currently down, and
while it was up it sometimes served two different builds alternately. Staging
and production have never released. Previews are unreliable. This plan names
the causes and fixes them.

Right now (from the probe you ran):

- `/` returns **503 with a fully rendered page** — that is `web`'s own
  `apiUnavailable` branch. The web container is healthy and doing its job.
- `/healthz`, `/readyz` and every `/api/v1/*` return **502 via Caddy** — Caddy
  is up and has no upstream. The api container is not accepting connections.

**Your OpenBao inference is wrong, and it is worth saying so before anything
is built on it.** `#591` is already merged to `main`
(`dd7bfc4`, `8d079d1`, `7a83698`) and the vault is **optional by
construction**: `cmd/apivo/vault.go:32-38` returns `nil, nil` when
`PAYOUT_VAULT_URL` is unset, and `cmd/apivo/main.go:769-776` documents that
as "not a failure" — `POST /payout-destinations` answers 503 and everything
else keeps working. A missing vault cannot stop the api booting. The
`xcoder/openbao-on-qa` branch is unmerged and is not implicated.

### What is certain, and what is inferred

- **Certain, from the code:** RC2, RC3, RC4 and RC5. Every claim is a line in
  this repository and none of them depends on host state.
- **Inferred:** that RC1 is what is killing QA *right now*. The signature
  matches exactly — `web` up, `api` absent, 502 on every api route — but a
  crash-loop, an OOM or an expired GHCR credential on the host would look the
  same from outside. Phase 0 settles it.
- **Wrong, and worth retiring:** OpenBao. See above.

An adversarial verification pass over these hypotheses is still running; if it
overturns anything, that lands as an amendment to this file rather than a
quiet edit.

---

## The five root causes

### RC1 — `api` is gated on Postgres; `web` is gated on nothing

`deploy/hetzner/compose/docker-compose.local-db.yml:97-102`

```yaml
  api:
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
```

`web` declares no `depends_on` at all
(`deploy/hetzner/compose/docker-compose.yml:75-146`).

If QA's Postgres is unhealthy or gone, compose **will not start the api**,
while `web` comes up regardless. Caddy then 502s `/api/v1/*`, `/healthz` and
`/readyz` (`deploy/hetzner/caddy/snippets.caddy:96-100`) and the web renders
its own 503. **That is exactly the signature you observed**, and it is the
first thing to check on the box.

### RC2 — a failed rollout rebuilds the *whole* stack, twice, every tick — this is the "two versions"

`deploy/hetzner/bin/apivo-reconcile:407-420` and `:451-465`.

`roll_out()` runs one `compose up -d --wait` over **both** services. When the
api fails, `roll_out` returns 1 and the rollback path calls `roll_out` **again**
with the previous digests — recreating `web` as well, which was never at
fault. Then:

- `record_state` never runs, so `current` still names the old digests
  (`:427`).
- The next timer tick (60 s, `apivo-reconcile@.timer:30`) sees
  `RUNNING_API != API_DIGEST` and rolls forward again.

So a broken api puts the environment into a **permanent oscillation**: web is
recreated on the new image, fails, is recreated on the old image, and repeats
every 1–4 minutes for as long as the channel points at the failing build. The
script's own message says the quiet part out loud (`:462`): *"The channel still
points at the broken build, so the next tick will try it again."* Nothing
remembers that a digest already failed, and nothing backs off.

**A reader refreshing during that cycle sees two different builds. That is the
"two versions at the same time".** It is not a proxy bug, not a cache, and not
a race — the host is genuinely alternating between them on a timer.

Ruled out by evidence: Caddy has exactly one upstream per handle and zero
load-balancing, retry or failover directives (`snippets.caddy:96-160`);
`container_name` is fixed everywhere so two versions cannot run concurrently
in one project; the Cloudflare Worker is deployed nowhere (`ci.yml:686-687`
is `--dry-run`).

### RC3 — images are automated; everything else on a host is not

`apivo-reconcile` converges **images only**. The Caddyfiles, every compose
file, the systemd units, and the reconciler scripts themselves are copied by
`deploy/hetzner/provision.sh`, which a human runs over SSH. No workflow ships
anything to a host — there is no ssh/scp/rsync step in `.github/workflows/`.

That makes every change under `deploy/hetzner/**` a silent no-op until someone
remembers. Concretely stale on any host provisioned before them:

- `snippets.caddy:96` — `/api/v1/*` instead of `/api/*` (#546, 2026-09-07).
- `docker-compose.yml:132` — the brand directory mount (#547).
- `docker-compose.edge.preprod.yml:33` — Caddy joining `preview-edge`. Its own
  comment records this exact regression: *"every preview answers 502 with its
  containers sitting there healthy."*
- `apivo-reconcile:166-169` — the web-certificate precondition.
- `apivo-previews:503-507` — pull-before-up, without which a preview serves
  its first commit forever.

Nothing detects the drift. `apivoctl status` reports containers, not config.

### RC4 — staging and production are gated shut by a committed empty string

`deploy/hetzner/environments.env:48` `APIVO_STAGING_URL=` and `:57`
`APIVO_PROD_URL=`. `release.yml:169-182` refuses any release to a channel whose
URL is empty, **before** verify and publish. So every `v*` tag push dies in the
`guard` job.

This is why only QA works. It is the intended guard doing its job — but
`docs/ENVIRONMENTS.md:24-26` says staging's host is provisioned and answering
on `https://reapie.com`, so the guard is now the only thing left. The repo has
**one tag ever** (`v0.1.0`, 2026-08-16) and `origin/main` is **1072 commits**
past it. Nothing downstream of a tag — semver validation, the approval, the
channel move, the probe — has ever executed.

### RC5 — the version identity is incoherent, so skew is undetectable

- `publish.yml:207-208` moves the two channel tags in **two separate calls**.
- `apivo-reconcile:338-341` guards that skew by comparing OCI labels — but
  `image_version()` (`:313-317`) falls back to the literal `dev` when the label
  is missing, so two unlabelled images compare **equal** and the guard passes.
- A half-completed channel move turns into a **permanent silent stall** at
  `exit 0`, once a minute, forever. Nothing escalates it.
- `publish.yml:183-193` proves only the **api** stamp. `web/Dockerfile` has no
  build-time stamp at all.
- The frontend's version is a **runtime env var** set from the *api* image's
  label (`apivo-reconcile:319,354` → `docker-compose.yml:94`). The running web
  bundle's own identity is never reported anywhere.
- `sha-<commit>` is documented as immutable (`publish.yml:18`) but is
  **overwritten** when a release tag lands on a commit already published from
  main (`publish.yml:155` uses `github.sha` on both paths).

All six phases land, in this order, as small PRs — each one building and
passing its own tests, one branch per issue under `xcoder/`.

```sh
docker logs --tail 100 apivo-qa-api
```

"two versions at the same time".** It is not a proxy bug, not a cache, and not
a race — the host is genuinely alternating between them on a timer.

Ruled out by evidence: Caddy has exactly one upstream per handle and zero
load-balancing, retry or failover directives (`snippets.caddy:96-160`);
`container_name` is fixed everywhere so two versions cannot run concurrently
in one project; the Cloudflare Worker is deployed nowhere (`ci.yml:686-687`
is `--dry-run`).

### RC3 — images are automated; everything else on a host is not

`apivo-reconcile` converges **images only**. The Caddyfiles, every compose
file, the systemd units, and the reconciler scripts themselves are copied by
`deploy/hetzner/provision.sh`, which a human runs over SSH. No workflow ships
anything to a host — there is no ssh/scp/rsync step in `.github/workflows/`.

That makes every change under `deploy/hetzner/**` a silent no-op until someone
remembers. Concretely stale on any host provisioned before them:

- `snippets.caddy:96` — `/api/v1/*` instead of `/api/*` (#546, 2026-09-07).
- `docker-compose.yml:132` — the brand directory mount (#547).
- `docker-compose.edge.preprod.yml:33` — Caddy joining `preview-edge`. Its own
  comment records this exact regression: *"every preview answers 502 with its
  containers sitting there healthy."*
- `apivo-reconcile:166-169` — the web-certificate precondition.
- `apivo-previews:503-507` — pull-before-up, without which a preview serves
  its first commit forever.

Nothing detects the drift. `apivoctl status` reports containers, not config.

### RC4 — staging and production are gated shut by a committed empty string

`deploy/hetzner/environments.env:48` `APIVO_STAGING_URL=` and `:57`
`APIVO_PROD_URL=`. `release.yml:169-182` refuses any release to a channel whose
URL is empty, **before** verify and publish. So every `v*` tag push dies in the
`guard` job.

This is why only QA works. It is the intended guard doing its job — but
`docs/ENVIRONMENTS.md:24-26` says staging's host is provisioned and answering
on `https://reapie.com`, so the guard is now the only thing left. The repo has
**one tag ever** (`v0.1.0`, 2026-08-16) and `origin/main` is **1072 commits**
past it. Nothing downstream of a tag — semver validation, the approval, the
channel move, the probe — has ever executed.

### RC5 — the version identity is incoherent, so skew is undetectable

- `publish.yml:207-208` moves the two channel tags in **two separate calls**.
- `apivo-reconcile:338-341` guards that skew by comparing OCI labels — but
  `image_version()` (`:313-317`) falls back to the literal `dev` when the label
  is missing, so two unlabelled images compare **equal** and the guard passes.
- A half-completed channel move turns into a **permanent silent stall** at
  `exit 0`, once a minute, forever. Nothing escalates it.
- `publish.yml:183-193` proves only the **api** stamp. `web/Dockerfile` has no
  build-time stamp at all.
- The frontend's version is a **runtime env var** set from the *api* image's
  label (`apivo-reconcile:319,354` → `docker-compose.yml:94`). The running web
  bundle's own identity is never reported anywhere.
- `sha-<commit>` is documented as immutable (`publish.yml:18`) but is
  **overwritten** when a release tag lands on a commit already published from
  main (`publish.yml:155` uses `github.sha` on both paths).

## The work

All six phases land, in this order, as small PRs — each one building and
passing its own tests, one branch per issue under `xcoder/`.

### Phase 0 — triage the box — **BLOCKING, and yours to run**

I have no shell on the VPS. Nothing below starts until this comes back,
because it decides whether RC1 is the cause or merely the most probable one.

```sh

docker ps -a --filter name=apivo-qa-
docker inspect --format '{{.State.Health.Status}}' apivo-qa-postgres
docker logs --tail 100 apivo-qa-postgres
docker logs --tail 100 apivo-qa-api
journalctl -u apivo-reconcile@qa --since '2 hours ago' | tail -60
cat /var/lib/apivo/qa/current /var/lib/apivo/qa/images.env
df -h && free -m                        # a full disk or OOM is the usual cause
```

The journal is JSON per line (`apivo-reconcile:55-62`); the lines that decide
this are `rollout_failed`, `rollback_failed`, `version_skew` and
`digest_mismatch`. Paste them back.

What each answer changes:

| Journal says | Confirms | Changes |
|---|---|---|
| `rollout_failed` then `rollback_failed`, repeating | RC1 + RC2 | Plan stands as written |
| `version_skew` once a minute | RC5, half-moved channel | Phase 4 moves ahead of Phase 1 |
| `registry` / `cannot resolve` | GHCR credential expired on the host | New cause; Phase 1 changes shape |
| Quiet ticks, api still down | Not the reconciler — a crash-loop or OOM | Phase 1 still lands but is not the fix |

Then re-run `provision.sh` on that host — it is idempotent — because RC3 means
it is very likely several fixes behind, `snippets.caddy:96` (#546) included.
`apivoctl resume qa` once the cause is named.

### Phase 1 — stop the oscillation (`deploy/hetzner/bin/apivo-reconcile`)

1. **Remember a failed digest and refuse to retry it.** Write the failing
   `API_DIGEST`/`WEB_DIGEST` pair to `$STATE_DIR/failed` on a rollout failure;
   at the top of the tick, if the resolved pair equals `failed`, log once and
   `exit 0`. Clear the file whenever the resolved pair differs. This turns
   "retry a known-bad build every minute forever" into "hold the last good
   version and say so".
2. **Do not roll `web` back when only `api` failed.** Have `roll_out` return
   *which* verification failed and restore only that service, so a healthy
   frontend is not recreated onto an older build. This is the direct fix for
   the two-versions symptom.
3. **Make the skew guard fail closed.** In `image_version()`, treat an absent
   label as an error rather than substituting `dev` — two unlabelled images
   must not compare equal. (Go's `index` returns the empty string for a
   missing map key, so `:315`'s `[ -n "$_v" ] || _v=dev` fires; a failed
   `docker image inspect` collapses to the same value via `|| true` at `:314`.
   Both roads lead to `dev == dev`, and the guard passes.)
4. **Escalate a persistent stall.** `version_skew` (`:338-341`) currently exits
   0 forever. After N consecutive skew ticks, exit non-zero so systemd marks
   the unit failed and the state is visible.

Extend `deploy/hetzner/bin/apivo-reconcile_test.sh` for each: it already stubs
the registry and the daemon, and already covers skew at `:331-351`.

### Phase 2 — close the config-delivery gap (RC3)

Add a **config revision** the host records and reports:

- `provision.sh` writes the checked-out commit to
  `/etc/apivo/config-revision` when it installs files.
- `apivoctl status` prints it beside the running versions.
- Optionally: `apivo-reconcile` compares it against a value carried in the api
  image's OCI labels and logs a warning when the host's deploy config is older
  than the build it is being asked to run.

This does not automate delivery — the no-SSH-from-CI property is deliberate and
worth keeping — it makes the drift *visible*, which is the actual defect.

Also add `APIVO_PREVIEW_DOMAIN` to `deploy/hetzner/env/edge.env.example` (it is
missing at `:39-48`, and `Caddyfile.preprod:81` uses it in a site address —
Caddy refuses to start on an unset site variable, which takes QA and staging
down with previews).

### Phase 3 — unblock staging, then production (RC4)

One PR, in this order:

1. Verify `https://reapie.com/healthz` answers from the host (it will 502 until
   a release lands — that is expected).
2. Set `APIVO_STAGING_URL=https://reapie.com` in
   `deploy/hetzner/environments.env:48`.
3. Cut `v0.2.0-rc.1` as an **annotated, signed** tag on a merged commit and let
   `release.yml` run end to end. This exercises the guard, the notes, the
   channel move and the probe for the first time.
4. Leave `APIVO_PROD_URL` empty until a production host exists. Confirm the
   `production` GitHub Environment exists **with reviewers** — `release.yml:206`
   names it, and if it does not exist the approval gate is decoration.

`docs/RELEASING.md:23` claims all three URLs are empty; QA's is not. Fix that
line in the same PR.

### Phase 4 — one coherent version identity (RC5) — taken in full

1. **Stamp the web at build time.** A `VERSION` build arg into
   `web/Dockerfile`, baked in as the `PUBLIC_APP_VERSION` default, so the
   image carries its own identity instead of being told one at runtime by
   `docker-compose.yml:94`. The compose env var stays as an override, so
   previews keep their `pr-<n>` stamp and `isPreviewVersion`
   (`web/src/lib/cashback/api.ts`) is unaffected.
2. **Prove both stamps.** Extend `publish.yml:183-193`, which today runs
   `docker run … api version` and nothing equivalent for the web. Give the web
   image a way to state its version without a browser (a `node -e` one-liner
   over the baked default, matching the healthcheck idiom already in
   `web/Dockerfile`).
3. **Make the channel move atomic-or-loud.** `publish.yml:207-208` are two
   `imagetools create` calls. Either move both under one step whose failure
   is fatal and names which tag moved, or move `web` first and `api` second so
   a half-move leaves the *api* — the thing `served_version` asserts against —
   still pointing at the proven pair.
4. **Fail the skew guard closed.** `image_version()`
   (`apivo-reconcile:313-317`) substitutes `dev` for a missing label *and* for
   a failed inspect, so two unlabelled images compare equal and the guard at
   `:338` passes. Treat an absent label as an error. (Same change as Phase 1
   item 3 — land it there, listed here for completeness.)
5. **Stop reusing `sha-<commit>`, and tag released images `v<semver>`.**
   `publish.yml:155` uses `github.sha` on both paths, so a release tag landing
   on a commit already published from main **overwrites** the `sha-<C>` tag
   with a differently stamped image — directly contradicting the immutability
   claim at `publish.yml:18` and `docs/architecture/cicd-architecture.md:456`.
   On the release path, push `v<semver>` as well, so a released artefact has an
   immutable name that is not a commit hash.
6. **Report both versions.** `scripts/env_status.sh:56-72` reads only
   `/healthz`. Add the web's, so "two versions" becomes a thing the tooling can
   *say* rather than something a human notices by refreshing. Update
   `release.yml`'s probe (`:362-375`) to check both.

### Phase 5 — previews

- Pin previews by **digest** like every named environment
  (`apivo-previews:361-362`, `:503-505` use mutable tags).
- Add `--wait` to the converge branch (`apivo-previews:513-516`); create uses it
  (`:372`) and converge does not, so a converge that starts a broken container
  reports success.
- Set `PREVIEW_CLEANUP_TOKEN` — without it `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot delete package
  versions (`preview.yml:57-68`), closed PRs keep their tags, and the cap
  (`APIVO_PREVIEW_MAX=5`, newest-first) evicts *live* previews in favour of dead
  ones.
- Check the Cloudflare wildcard `*.ra1ze.com` is **orange-clouded**.
  `docs/RUNBOOK.md:107-113` records this exact failure: a grey-clouded wildcard
  sends the browser to the VPS IP, which the firewall admits only from
  Cloudflare ranges — *"the symptom is previews timing out while QA works."*
- Call `k8s-topology.yml` and `make-targets.yml` from `publish.yml`; both
  declare `workflow_call` and nothing calls them, so they gate pull requests but
  not the path that deploys to QA (`k8s-topology.yml:20-25` admits this).

### Phase 6 — documentation that currently contradicts itself

`docs/ENVIRONMENTS.md:124` (previews "point at nothing at all") vs `:588` and
the code; `README.md:146-150` (QA "not yet" provisioned) vs
`ENVIRONMENTS.md:17,20`; `RELEASING.md:208-209` (one Supabase project) vs
`ENVIRONMENTS.md:63-67` (two). `deploy/k8s/*-deployment.yaml` reference
`:latest`, a tag nothing writes.

```sh
sh deploy/hetzner/bin/apivo-reconcile_test.sh
sh deploy/hetzner/bin/apivo-previews_test.sh

```

The reconciler suite stubs the registry and the docker daemon, so Phase 1 is

failing digest is refused, a healthy `web` is not recreated when only `api`

**On the host, after Phase 0/2:**


## What I found

**The "two versions" is not a mystery — the host is genuinely alternating between two builds on a timer.**

Forward → fail → back → fail → forward, every 1–4 minutes, for as long as the channel points at a build the api can't run. The script's own message admits it: *"the next tick will try it again."* Nothing remembers a digest already failed.

WEB_A="sha256:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"
WEB_B="sha256:bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb"
REGISTRY="ghcr.io/nomos-n4s/apivo-news"

FAILS=0

# Reset to the happy path: a fresh QA environment tracking a registry that
# serves DIGEST_A/WEB_A as v0.1.0, and a daemon that does as it is told.
reset() {
    rm -rf "$APIVO_ETC" "$APIVO_STATE" "$STUB_DIR"
    mkdir -p "$APIVO_ETC/qa" "$APIVO_STATE" "$STUB_DIR"
    cat > "$APIVO_ETC/qa/stack.env" <<EOF
APIVO_ENV=qa
APIVO_CHANNEL=qa
APIVO_REGISTRY=$REGISTRY
COMPOSE_FILE=/opt/apivo/compose/docker-compose.yml
EOF
    # The frontend's certificate. A provisioned host has one; the reconciler
    # refuses to converge without it, because the container reads both files
    # at startup and dies if they are absent (see the check in apivo-reconcile).
    # Contents are never read here - only the reconciler's stat is.
    mkdir -p "$APIVO_ETC/qa/web-certs"
    : > "$APIVO_ETC/qa/web-certs/web.crt"
    : > "$APIVO_ETC/qa/web-certs/web.key"
    printf '%s' "$DIGEST_A" > "$STUB_DIR/digest_api"
    printf '%s' "$WEB_A" > "$STUB_DIR/digest_web"
    printf '%s' 'v0.1.0' > "$STUB_DIR/label_version"
}

# Bring the environment to a known-good running state, so a test can then
# break the NEXT rollout and observe the rollback. The call counter is reset
# afterwards, so a test's compose_exits always describes the rollouts it is
# actually about rather than counting from the fixture that set it up.
settle() {
    sh "$RECONCILE" qa >/dev/null 2>&1
    rm -f "$STUB_DIR/up_count"
}

run() {
    # run <env> - captures stdout+stderr and the exit code, never aborts.
    set +e
    OUT=$(sh "$RECONCILE" "$1" 2>&1)
    RC=$?
    set -e
}

check() {
    # check <description> <expected-rc> <required-output-fragment>
    if [ "$RC" -ne "$2" ]; then
        echo "FAIL: $1 - expected exit $2, got $RC: $OUT"
        FAILS=1
        return
    fi
    if [ -n "$3" ] && ! printf '%s' "$OUT" | grep -q -F -e "$3"; then
        echo "FAIL: $1 - exit $2 as expected, but the output never said '$3': $OUT"
        FAILS=1
        return
    fi
    echo "ok: $1"
}

check_state() {
    # check_state <description> <key> <expected>
    got=$(sed -n "s/^$2=//p" "$APIVO_STATE/qa/current" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)
    if [ "$got" != "$3" ]; then
        echo "FAIL: $1 - current $2 is '${got:-unset}', expected '$3'"
        FAILS=1
    else
        echo "ok: $1"
    fi
}

check_pinned() {
    # check_pinned <description> <expected-api-ref>
    got=$(sed -n 's/^APIVO_API_IMAGE=//p' "$STUB_IMAGES_ENV" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ "$got" != "$2" ]; then
        echo "FAIL: $1 - compose is pinned to '${got:-nothing}', expected '$2'"
        FAILS=1
    else
        echo "ok: $1"
    fi
}

# ===========================================================================
# Configuration refusals. Nothing is attempted, and the exit code says so
# (2, not 1): a misconfigured unit has not failed a deploy, it has failed to
# describe one.
# ===========================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The stub docker.
#
# It models just enough of a daemon and a registry to make the reconciler's
# decisions observable: which digest a tag resolves to, whether a rollout
# succeeds, and what the containers claim to be running afterwards. Its
# default behaviour is the happy path, so each test states only its own
# deviation from it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
cat > "$TMP/docker" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/sh
echo "$*" >> "$STUB_DIR/calls"
read_or() { [ -r "$STUB_DIR/$1" ] && cat "$STUB_DIR/$1" || printf '%s' "$2"; }
case "$1" in
buildx)
    # buildx imagetools inspect <ref> --format <fmt>
    #
    # Faithful to buildx v0.31.1, including its trap: a --format BEGINNING
    # with `{{.Manifest` is ignored and the human-readable block is printed
    # instead. Modelling that is the whole point - the previous stub `cat`ed a
    # bare digest whatever the format, so it proved the reconciler handles a
    # digest correctly and never that it obtains one. The real script shipped
    # unable to resolve a single digest, and this suite stayed green.
    # buildx can also FAIL rather than print an empty digest, and the two are
    # not the same event. The first host ever provisioned hit the failure: the
    # systemd sandbox left $HOME read-only and buildx could not create its
    # state directory. The reconciler discarded that message and reported its
    # generic "cannot resolve", whose suggested causes were all wrong, while a
    # `docker pull` by hand worked perfectly.
    if [ -s "$STUB_DIR/buildx_error" ]; then
        cat "$STUB_DIR/buildx_error" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    case "$6" in
    '{{.Manifest'*)
        printf 'Name:      %s\nMediaType: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json\nDigest:    sha256:deadbeef\nManifests:\n' "$4"
        ;;
    *)
        case "$4" in
        */api:*) read_or digest_api '' ;;
        */web:*) read_or digest_web '' ;;
        esac
        ;;
    esac
    ;;
pull)
    [ -e "$STUB_DIR/pull_fails" ] && exit 1
    exit 0
    ;;
image)
    case "$2" in
    # The version the release pipeline stamped into the image as an OCI label.
    # api and web are answered separately so a test can present the mismatched
    # pair that a half-moved channel produces.
    inspect)
        case "$5" in
        */web@*) read_or web_label_version "$(read_or label_version 'v0.1.0')" ;;
        *) read_or label_version 'v0.1.0' ;;
        esac
        ;;
    prune) : ;;
    esac
    ;;
container)
    # container inspect --format '{{.Config.Image}}' <name>
    # Answers with whatever the reconciler most recently pinned, which is what
    # a real daemon would say after a successful rollout. A test that wants a
    # container stuck on the old image writes running_override.
    # PER CONTAINER. A single override answered both, so no test could hold
    # exactly one container stale - and with both stale, deleting either of
    # the reconciler's two verify calls still left the suite green. Each check
    # is only genuinely covered when the other one passes.
    case "$5" in
    *-api)
        if [ -e "$STUB_DIR/running_override_api" ]; then

    # version that was deployed, so that is what the pin says.

        # succeeds". Past the end of the file, everything succeeds.

        ;;

input.command:
gh api repos/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/issues -f title="A failed rollout is retried every minute forever, flipping the frontend between two versions" -F body="$(cat <<'EOF'
## What happens

When a rollout fails, `apivo-reconcile` rolls back and exits. Nothing records
that the digest pair it just tried is broken, so the next timer tick — sixty
seconds later — resolves the same channel, sees `current` still naming the old
digests, and rolls forward again. Forward, fail, back, fail, forward.

Every cycle recreates **both** containers twice. The frontend is therefore
alternating between two builds on a one-minute timer, while the api never comes
up. A reader refreshing the site sees two different versions of the application.

Observed on QA, 2026-09-07:

```
22:13:15  container apivo-qa-api is unhealthy
22:13:16  {"event":"rollout_failed","msg":"rolling back qa to the previous digest"}
22:13:16  Container apivo-qa-api Recreate
22:13:16  Container apivo-qa-web Recreate      <- never at fault
22:13:29  container apivo-qa-api is unhealthy
22:13:29  {"event":"rollback_failed","msg":"... qa is DOWN and no automatic path remains"}
22:14:04  Starting apivo-reconcile@qa.service...
22:14:08  {"event":"rollout_start","msg":"qa moved: api ...212f82c -> ...b036c0e, web ...b857450 -> ...d05da16"}
22:14:12  Container apivo-qa-api Recreate
22:14:12  Container apivo-qa-web Recreate
```

`deploy/hetzner/bin/apivo-reconcile:462` states the behaviour plainly — *"The
channel still points at the broken build, so the next tick will try it again"* —
but a retry that recreates the whole stack every minute indefinitely is not a
retry, it is a churn loop that takes the frontend with it.

## Why it matters beyond the noise

The rollback is not free. It stops and recreates the web container, which is
healthy and correct, in order to keep the api/web pair matched. Doing that once
per failed deploy is right. Doing it forever means the one environment agents
look at serves an unpredictable version, and the container logs that would
explain the failure are rotated away by the churn.

## Two adjacent defects found alongside it

- **`image_version()` fails open.** `apivo-reconcile:313-317` substitutes the
  literal `dev` both when the OCI version label is absent and when
  `docker image inspect` fails outright. Two unlabelled images therefore compare
  equal, and the half-moved-channel guard at `:338` passes on a mismatched pair —
  the exact case it exists to catch.
- **A persistent version skew never escalates.** `:338-341` exits 0 once a
  minute forever. If `publish.yml` half-fails — it moves the two channel tags in
  two separate calls at `publish.yml:207-208` — the environment stalls silently
  and nothing ever says so.

## Proposed fix

1. Record a failed digest pair in `$STATE_DIR/failed`, written **before** the
   rollback is attempted. On a later tick, if the channel still resolves to that
   pair, keep the stack self-healing with `compose up -d` but refuse to roll
   forward again, and fail loudly. Clear the record the moment the channel names
   something else.
2. Make `image_version()` fail closed: an absent label or a failed inspect is an
   error naming the image, not `dev`.
3. Escalate a version skew that persists beyond a few ticks, so a half-moved
   channel stops being silent.

`deploy/hetzner/bin/apivo-reconcile_test.sh` already stubs the registry and the
daemon and can prove all three without a host.
EOF
)" --jq '.number, .html_url'

import io

s = io.open(p, encoding='utf-8', newline=None).read()
orig = s

# --- Hunk 1: the state path -------------------------------------------------
old = 'IMAGES_ENV="$STATE_DIR/images.env"\n'
new = '''IMAGES_ENV="$STATE_DIR/images.env"
# The digest pair whose rollout failed, so that it is attempted ONCE rather
# than once a minute forever. The refusal below is what that file buys.
FAILED="$STATE_DIR/failed"
'''
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)

# --- Hunk 2: record_failed, beside record_state -----------------------------
old = '''record_state() {
'''
new = '''record_failed() {
    # record_failed <api-digest> <web-digest>
    #
    # Written BEFORE the rollback is attempted, not after it. A rollback can
    # itself hang and be killed at TimeoutStartSec, and that is precisely the
    # case where retrying the same broken pair costs the most - so the record
    # has to survive this process not reaching its own end.
    _tmp="$FAILED.new"
    {
        echo "# Written by apivo-reconcile: this pair failed to roll out."
        echo "API_DIGEST=$1"
        echo "WEB_DIGEST=$2"
        echo "AT=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
    } > "$_tmp"
    mv "$_tmp" "$FAILED"
}

record_state() {
'''
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)

# --- Hunk 3: the refusal, after the quiet path ------------------------------
old = '''log info rollout_start "$APIVO_CHANNEL moved: api ${RUNNING_API:-none} -> $API_DIGEST, web ${RUNNING_WEB:-none} -> $WEB_DIGEST"
'''
new = '''# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The pair that already failed.
#
# A failed rollout rolls back and exits, and nothing about the registry
# changes: the channel still names the build that could not come up. Sixty
# seconds later this script resolves the same pair, finds `current` still
# naming the old digests - `record_state` never ran - and rolls forward into
# the identical failure. Forward, fail, back, fail, forward.
#
# Each cycle recreates BOTH containers twice, because the rollback restores
# the pair rather than the one service that broke. So a frontend that was
# never at fault is stopped and restarted on alternating builds for as long
# as the channel points at a broken api, and a reader refreshing the site
# sees two different versions of the application. That is how this was
# found. The churn also rotates away the container logs that would have
# explained the original failure.
#
# Attempting it once is a retry. Attempting it every minute forever is a
# churn loop wearing a retry's clothes.
#
# `up -d` still runs, because a refusal must not cost the self-healing
# property the quiet path above exists for - but nothing is pulled, nothing
# is recreated, and the environment holds the last version that served.
#
# This is not a latch anybody has to remember to release: the record is
# cleared the moment the channel names a different pair, so a fix pushed to
# main is taken on the next tick with no manual step. It is a statement about
# one digest pair, and it expires when that pair does.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FAILED_API=$(read_state_field "$FAILED" API_DIGEST)
FAILED_WEB=$(read_state_field "$FAILED" WEB_DIGEST)

if [ -n "$FAILED_API" ] && { [ "$FAILED_API" != "$API_DIGEST" ] || [ "$FAILED_WEB" != "$WEB_DIGEST" ]; }; then
    rm -f "$FAILED"
    FAILED_API=""
fi

if [ -n "$FAILED_API" ]; then
    # Self-healing first, refusal second. images.env still pins whatever last
    # served, so a container that died between ticks comes back even while
    # this environment is held.
    compose up -d --remove-orphans >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    die rollout_refused "$APIVO_CHANNEL points at api $API_DIGEST and web $WEB_DIGEST, whose rollout already failed; it is not being retried. $ENV_NAME keeps serving ${RUNNING_VERSION:-the digests in $CURRENT}. Read why it failed with 'docker compose logs', then fix it forward - this refusal clears itself as soon as the channel names a different pair." 1
fi

log info rollout_start "$APIVO_CHANNEL moved: api ${RUNNING_API:-none} -> $API_DIGEST, web ${RUNNING_WEB:-none} -> $WEB_DIGEST"
'''
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)

# --- Hunk 4: RUNNING_VERSION, for the refusal message -----------------------
old = '''RUNNING_WEB=$(read_state_field "$CURRENT" WEB_DIGEST)
'''
new = '''RUNNING_WEB=$(read_state_field "$CURRENT" WEB_DIGEST)
RUNNING_VERSION=$(read_state_field "$CURRENT" VERSION)
'''
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)

# --- Hunk 5: poison the pair before rolling back ----------------------------
old = '''log error rollout_failed "rolling back $ENV_NAME to the previous digest"
'''
new = '''record_failed "$API_DIGEST" "$WEB_DIGEST"
log error rollout_failed "rolling back $ENV_NAME to the previous digest"
'''
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)

# --- Hunk 6: a proven pair is not poisoned ----------------------------------
old = '''    record_state "$CURRENT" "$API_DIGEST" "$WEB_DIGEST" "$IMAGE_VERSION"
'''
new = '''    record_state "$CURRENT" "$API_DIGEST" "$WEB_DIGEST" "$IMAGE_VERSION"
    # Belt and braces. The refusal above already clears a record naming a
    # different pair, and one naming THIS pair would have refused before
    # reaching here - but a state directory nobody can explain is worse than
    # an unlink that usually does nothing.
    rm -f "$FAILED"
'''
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)

assert s != orig
io.open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\r\n').write(s)
print('6 hunks applied')

fix(deploy): a failed rollout is tried once, not once a minute forever (#604)

A rollout that fails rolls back and exits, and nothing about the registry
changes: the channel still names the build that could not come up. Sixty
seconds later the reconciler resolved the same pair, found `current` still
naming the old digests - `record_state` never ran - and rolled forward into
the identical failure. Forward, fail, back, fail, forward.

Each cycle recreated BOTH containers twice, because the rollback restores the
pair rather than the one service that broke. A frontend that was never at
fault was stopped and restarted onto alternating builds for as long as the
channel pointed at a broken api, so the site served two different versions of
itself - which is how this was found. The churn also rotated away the
container logs that would have explained the original failure.

Attempting it once is a retry. Attempting it every minute forever is a churn
loop wearing a retry's clothes.

The pair is now recorded BEFORE the rollback is attempted, so it survives a
rollback that itself hangs and is killed at TimeoutStartSec - precisely the
case where retrying costs the most - and it is refused on every later tick.
`up -d` still runs, because the refusal must not cost the self-healing
property the quiet path exists for, but nothing is pulled and nothing is
recreated.

It is not a latch nobody can release: the record is cleared the moment the
channel names a different pair, so a fix pushed to main is taken on the next
tick with no manual step.

The `rolled_back` message promised a retry that no longer happens, so it now
says what does.

restores the pair rather than the one service that broke. The pair is now
recorded *before* the rollback is attempted, so it survives a rollback that
hangs and is killed at `TimeoutStartSec`, and refused afterwards. `up -d` still
runs, so the self-healing property the quiet path exists for is untouched. The
record clears itself the moment the channel names a different pair, so a fix

refusal names which of the two it was; a skew past tolerance escalates.

says what does — and its assertion changed with it.

cause is environmental rather than a bad build. This stops the churn and holds

## The two-versions mystery is solved — your journal is the proof

RC2 confirmed exactly. The rollback recreates the frontend that was never at fault, `record_state` never runs, so `current` still names the old digests, and 35 seconds later systemd starts the whole thing again. Your web was flipping between `b857450…` and `d05da16…` every minute.

```
images.env:  APIVO_VERSION=main-e648b2e   (what it keeps trying)
```

The fix records a failed pair *before* the rollback is attempted — so it survives a rollback killed at `TimeoutStartSec` — and refuses it afterwards, while still running `up -d` so self-healing is untouched. It clears itself when the channel moves on, so it's not a latch anyone has to remember to release.

## I was wrong about RC1 — Postgres is fine

I predicted `depends_on: service_healthy` was blocking the api. It isn't:

```
Container apivo-qa-postgres  Healthy
Container apivo-qa-api       Starting
Container apivo-qa-api       Started
container apivo-qa-api is unhealthy      ← one second later
```

The api *starts* and dies immediately, on **both** images. Failing identically on two different builds rules out the build. Disk 78% with 16G free, 6.4G memory available — not exhaustion either.

And `/etc/apivo/qa/api.env` is hand-maintained, which is where "someone mid-flight replacing how QA delivers secrets" lands.

So your instinct about the OpenBao work was right about *relevance* and wrong about *mechanism*: the merged vault code is optional and can't stop a boot, but a half-edited `api.env` breaks every image equally — which is exactly why the rollback failed too.
